open_questions/0.rationale: Both arms are supported, and the evidence for each is of a different kind. Both arms are now mechanistically described, which is a change from how this was framed until recently. The pore's prepore and pore states are resolved by cryo-EM to 3.1 and 3.7 Angstrom respectively, and the channel's conductance is measured. The receptor arm has its own delineated cascade - latrophilin-1 to Gaq-phospholipase C to IP3 to store release to store-operated calcium entry - established with a pore-deficient toxin mutant in latrophilin-1 knockout mice, which is the cleanest available way to isolate it from the pore. What remains open is not whether either arm exists but what each contributes in a human envenomation. The receptor cascade was characterised for spontaneous quantal release at the mouse neuromuscular junction, not for the massive discharge of latrodectism; all of the discriminating work is in cultured cells, synaptosomes and mice; and nothing in the clinical picture distinguishes the two.

evidence.explanation: Bears directly on the species explanation, and against it: the Australian antivenom neutralises both American species' venom in a mouse model, so species difference alone is a weak account of why the two trials disagree. The species names are the point of the quote, which is why the whole sentence is given.

open_questions/1.rationale: RAVE-II randomised 224 patients against placebo on top of standardised analgesia and found no significant benefit. Dart and colleagues randomised 60 patients against placebo and met their primary endpoint. Four candidate explanations remain, and the entry cannot choose between them: a different spider and a different antivenom product (Latrodectus hasselti in Australia versus L. mactans in the United States - the products' antibody formats are not described in either trial abstract, so no comparison of them is asserted here); a different primary endpoint (pain improvement at 2 hours versus sustained reduction over 48 hours); a fourfold difference in size, with RAVE-II's confidence interval only just crossing zero; and the fact that RAVE-II gave both arms standardised analgesia first, which is a harder comparator to beat. The species explanation is the weakest of the four: redback antivenom neutralises L. mactans venom in a mouse model, so the two products are not obviously aimed at incomparable targets. The practical question - whether to give a product that causes systemic hypersensitivity in about 1 in 28 recipients, and that killed a patient in the largest published series - turns on the answer.

steps/1.description: NOGGIN is a secreted antagonist that sequesters BMPs and GDFs, setting the level of BMP signal a tissue receives. Loss-of-function NOG alleles cause joint-fusion phenotypes — proximal symphalangism, multiple synostoses, stapes ankylosis — but not brachydactyly. The BDB2 variants behave differently: free-binding-energy calculations for the modelled NOG-GDF5 complex and micromass functional assays do not indicate a major loss of function, so the interpretation is a subtle shift in which ligands NOG binds and how tightly, tilting the BMP balance rather than removing the brake. That distinction is what explains why these alleles add terminal digital deficiency to the familiar NOG joint phenotype.

steps/2.description: BMP signalling both drives chondrocyte differentiation within the digital condensation and specifies where the interzone forms that will become a joint. Shifting the balance therefore hits two things at once: segments fail to form distally (brachydactyly) and joints fail to cavitate proximally (symphalangism, carpal synostosis). The clinical combination in BDB2 — proximal joint fusion together with terminal digital deficiency — is the human read-out of that dual effect, and the authors read it as evidence that the ROR2 and BMP receptor pathways are functionally connected, plausibly via a heteromeric receptor complex at the cell surface.

steps/4.description: Brucella is a facultative intracellular pathogen that survives and replicates within host phagocytes (chiefly macrophages). This intracellular lifestyle shields the organism from antibodies and complement and, critically for therapy, from antibiotics that cannot accumulate inside eukaryotic cells — notably the beta-lactams. Effective treatment is therefore restricted to cell-penetrant agents (doxycycline, aminoglycosides that concentrate at the site, rifampicin), and cure requires prolonged combination therapy to reach and clear the protected intracellular reservoir. This is the lifestyle-gating principle that constrains drug choice beyond any single molecular target.

Human-to-human transmission is anecdotal, so essentially every human case begins at an animal reservoir. This is the proximal step the rest of this entry assumes: every other pathophysiology node here is downstream of established infection.

steps/18.description: Efficacy against the intracellular Brucella reservoir tracks the intracellular concentration a drug achieves, not merely its in vitro MIC. Doxycycline, rifampicin, and aminoglycosides accumulate within (or otherwise reach) infected cells, whereas beta-lactams do not — so the mainstay regimens are built from cell-penetrant agents given in prolonged combination. This is the cell-penetrant-drug requirement that the brucellosis treatments target.

steps/19.description: Brucella, like other bacteria, depends on 70S-ribosome translation of its mRNA. Doxycycline (a tetracycline) binds the 30S subunit and blocks aminoacyl-tRNA delivery, and the aminoglycosides streptomycin and gentamicin also target the 30S ribosome — the shared molecular target that anchors the doxycycline-plus-aminoglycoside brucellosis regimens. This is a bacterial target absent from the beta-lactam-inaccessible host cytoplasm, complementing the intracellular-niche gating node.

steps/20.description: Rifampicin, a component of the classic WHO-recommended doxycycline-rifampicin regimen, binds the beta subunit of bacterial DNA-dependent RNA polymerase and blocks nascent-transcript elongation. Because rifamycins are cell- and tissue-penetrant, this target is reachable in the intracellular Brucella reservoir; single rpoB point mutations confer high-level resistance, which is part of why rifampicin is used in combination rather than alone.

steps/4.description: MKRN3 and DLK1 are both expressed only from the paternal allele, and both act to hold the hypothalamic GnRH pulse generator quiescent through childhood. Hypothalamic Mkrn3 transcript is abundant in the arcuate nucleus of prepubertal mice and falls immediately before puberty, so withdrawal of this brake is part of the normal pubertal trigger. A paternally transmitted loss-of-function variant in either gene removes the brake before the normal age of puberty; in the family in which the DLK1 defect was found, the deletion removed the DLK1 translational start site and left circulating DLK1 undetectable in every affected member.

steps/6.description: The central event in CPP is premature reawakening of the hypothalamic GnRH pulse generator. Hypothalamic GnRH neurons resume high-amplitude pulsatile GnRH secretion before the normal age of puberty, driving pituitary gonadotropin release. Upstream kisspeptin (KISS1/KISS1R) signaling stimulates GnRH neurons, while inhibitory factors including the paternally expressed imprinted genes MKRN3 and DLK1 normally restrain the axis during childhood; loss of this restraint or gain of kisspeptin tone triggers premature secretion.

evidence.snippet: Recent evidence describing the pathogenesis of and risk factors for CSC focuses on possible dysfunction of the choroid and retinal pigment epithelium, and the role of corticosteroids. It is suggested that CSC lies within the spectrum of pachychoroid disorders that share the characteristic of thickened choroidal tissue.
evidence.explanation: 2025 international expert review directly implicates corticosteroids and choroid-RPE dysfunction in CSCR pathogenesis, consistent with the mineralocorticoid receptor mechanism.

evidence.snippet: It is believed that the predominant pathway in CSCR is the mineralocorticoid pathway
evidence.explanation: 2023 comprehensive review states the mineralocorticoid pathway is believed to be the predominant pathway in CSCR, directly supporting this node's mechanism.

steps/0.description: Elevated glucocorticoids and mineralocorticoids—from exogenous corticosteroid use, endogenous hypercortisolism, or stress-driven neuroendocrine activation— overstimulate mineralocorticoid receptors (MR; encoded by NR3C2) in choroidal endothelial cells. This upregulates vascular permeability factors, disrupts endothelial tight junctions, and promotes choroidal congestion. NR3C2 variants have been associated with CSCR in candidate-gene haplotype studies (not genome-wide significant in the cited GWAS), linking genetic predisposition to the glucocorticoid/mineralocorticoid axis. Corticosteroid use is the strongest and most consistently documented modifiable environmental risk factor for CSCR, producing more severe disease with higher recurrence and bilateral involvement.

evidence.snippet: CSCR is the first ever described pachychoroid disease. Most recently, hypothetical venous overload choroidopathy is also proposed due to its distinguished morphological and pathological characteristics, including choroidal thickening, choriocapillaris hyperpermeability, remodelling, and intervortex venous anastomoses.
evidence.explanation: Landmark 2023 review establishes choroidal hyperpermeability and pachychoroid anatomy as the defining pathological feature of CSCR and introduces the venous overload choroidopathy model.

evidence.snippet: Abnormal choroidal veins in central serous chorioretinopathy patients have been shown to have similarities with varicose veins.
evidence.explanation: 2025 Nature Communications study links the abnormal choroidal venous remodeling of CSCR to varicose-vein biology, supporting the venous overload choroidopathy model of this node.

evidence.snippet: This was conﬁrmed in a meta-analysis of 2,452 patients and 865,767 controls from 4 studies (odds ratio=3.06, P = 7.4 × 10-15).
evidence.explanation: Meta-analytic confirmation of the PTPRB (VE-PTP) missense variant rs113791087 association with CSCR, directly linking vascular endothelial phosphatase dysfunction to the choroidal vascular pathology of this node. The quoted sentence's "This" refers to the FinnGen association of rs113791087 in PTPRB with CSC reported in the preceding abstract sentence.

steps/1.description: The primary anatomical and vascular event in CSCR is choroidal hyperpermeability with thickening and dilation of the choroid, especially in Haller's outer vascular layer (pachyvessels). Choriocapillaris hyperpermeability and attenuation of the inner layers (Sattler's layer) follow. CSCR is classified as the first described pachychoroid spectrum disease, a group characterized by dilated outer choroidal vessels driving pressure-mediated choriocapillaris dysfunction. Intervortex venous anastomoses and choroidal venous congestion may reflect underlying vascular endothelial phosphatase (VE-PTP; PTPRB) dysfunction and abnormal choroidal venous drainage, supporting the recently proposed "venous overload choroidopathy" hypothesis.

evidence.snippet: Protein QTL also suggested the protein-level contribution of the complement factor H pathway to CSC pathogenesis.
evidence.explanation: 2025 multi-ethnic GWAS meta-analysis (8,811 discovery, 4,338 replication) supports protein-level contribution of the CFH pathway to CSCR pathogenesis via protein quantitative trait locus analysis.

evidence.snippet: 26 CFH- or CFHRs-related pathways showed significant associations
evidence.explanation: ToppGene functional enrichment analysis of the genes mapped from the GWAS meta-analysis found 26 CFH- or CFHR-related pathways significantly associated with CSCR; these are pathway-enrichment associations, not genome-wide significant loci.

steps/2.description: Genetic variation at the CFH locus (1q31.3) is among the most consistently replicated susceptibility signals for CSCR across multiple GWAS. Complement factor H (CFH) and its related proteins (CFHR1-5) regulate the alternative complement pathway through competition for C3b binding. Functional enrichment analysis of genes mapped from GWAS meta-analysis identified 26 CFH- or CFHR-related pathways significantly associated with CSCR. Protein quantitative trait loci analyses support protein-level contribution of the CFH pathway to CSCR pathogenesis. The mechanism likely involves local complement dysregulation in the choroidal-RPE interface, driving tissue damage and chronic vascular inflammation, in parallel with the mineralocorticoid pathway.

evidence.snippet: In both acute and chronic CSCR, low serum LCN2 and NGAL/MMP-9, provide a biological link between the two CSCR forms, and potential susceptibility to oxidative stress and innate immune dysregulation in CSCR.
evidence.explanation: Case-control study in 147 CSCR patients demonstrates significantly reduced serum LCN2 across both CSCR subtypes, implicating oxidative stress susceptibility and innate immune dysregulation as contributors to RPE barrier failure.

steps/3.description: Hydrostatic and complement-mediated stress from the congested pachychoroid leads to focal RPE breakdown. RPE cells lose tight junction integrity and ion transport function, allowing fluid to leak through focal RPE defects into the subretinal space, visible as fluorescein angiography leakage points. In acute CSCR, single focal leaks predominate; in chronic CSCR, diffuse RPE atrophy and decompensation develop. Reduced serum lipocalin 2 (LCN2/NGAL) in CSCR patients reflects susceptibility to excessive oxidative stress and innate immune dysregulation, compounding RPE barrier failure.

evidence.snippet: Half-dose photodynamic therapy (PDT) remains the mainstay of clinical practice, with about 95% of patients with chronic CSCR improving to visual acuity (VA) of 20/30 or better.
evidence.explanation: Comprehensive review documents the visual prognosis of chronic CSCR with and without treatment, confirming subretinal fluid-driven photoreceptor injury as the primary determinant of visual outcomes.

steps/4.description: Fluid accumulation beneath the neurosensory retina separates the photoreceptor layer from the RPE, disrupting outer segment renewal, nutritional exchange, and visual signal transduction. Photoreceptor outer segments elongate abnormally in response to subretinal fluid; the ellipsoidal zone (EZ) band disruption on OCT correlates directly with visual acuity loss. Prolonged detachment in chronic CSCR leads to progressive photoreceptor atrophy, ganglion cell loss, and permanent visual impairment. Choroidal neovascularization (CNV; type 1) develops in 2–15.6% of chronic CSCR eyes and further threatens visual prognosis. Legal blindness develops in approximately 12.8% of patients after mean 11.3-year follow-up.

edges/0.description: MR overstimulation in choroidal endothelial cells upregulates vascular permeability factors and disrupts tight junctions, causing choroidal congestion and hyperpermeability.

edges/1.description: Increased hydrostatic pressure from congested choroidal vessels overwhelms RPE pump capacity and tight junction integrity, causing focal RPE breakdown and sub-RPE fluid accumulation.

edges/2.description: Complement dysregulation at the choroid-RPE interface promotes local inflammation and tissue injury, compounding the hydrostatic stress from choroidal hyperpermeability to drive RPE decompensation.

edges/3.description: Focal RPE breakdown allows transudation of fluid from the sub-RPE space into the subretinal compartment, creating the neurosensory retinal detachment that is the defining anatomical lesion of CSCR.

evidence.snippet: We propose a step-wise chart for clinical decision-making in the management and treatment of CSC. New data on long-term visual outcomes and the pathogenesis of CSC in relation to the pachychoroid disease spectrum provide a better understanding to inform our management of this disease.
evidence.explanation: 2025 international expert consensus proposes a step-wise management algorithm in which observation with risk factor modification is the initial strategy for uncomplicated acute CSCR.

treatments/0.description: First-line approach for acute CSCR, as approximately 90–95% of cases spontaneously resolve within 2–3 months. Observation includes: discontinuation of corticosteroids when possible, management of psychosocial stress, treatment of obstructive sleep apnea, and close monitoring with OCT and visual acuity assessments at 4–6 week intervals. Intervention is considered if SRF persists beyond 3–4 months or if the patient has special visual demands. Recurrence rates remain 15–50% after resolution, higher without treatment.

evidence.snippet: Half-dose photodynamic therapy (PDT) remains the mainstay of clinical practice, with about 95% of patients with chronic CSCR improving to visual acuity (VA) of 20/30 or better.
evidence.explanation: Comprehensive 2023 review establishes half-dose PDT as the mainstay treatment for chronic CSCR, with approximately 95% of patients achieving VA 20/30 or better.

evidence.snippet: Available evidence supports half-dose (or half-fluence) verteporfin photodynamic therapy as the treatment of choice for CSC to reduce choroidal hyperpermeability.
evidence.explanation: 2025 international expert consensus review recommends half-dose/half-fluence PDT as the treatment of choice for CSCR, targeting the underlying choroidal hyperpermeability.

treatments/1.description: Half-dose (3 mg/m² instead of 6 mg/m²) photodynamic therapy with verteporfin is the established treatment of choice for chronic CSCR. Verteporfin selectively accumulates in abnormal choroidal vessels; laser activation at 689 nm induces choriocapillaris vascular remodeling, reducing choroidal hyperpermeability and subretinal fluid accumulation. Half-dose protocol minimizes RPE damage compared to standard PDT. SRF resolution rates of 91% at 19 months of follow-up are reported; approximately 95% of treated patients achieve VA of 20/30 or better. PDT reduces recurrence to approximately 20% versus 53.8% with observation alone. The PLACE randomized trial demonstrated superiority of half-dose PDT over high-density subthreshold micropulse laser in chronic CSCR. Half-fluence PDT is an alternative reduced dosing strategy with comparable safety.

treatments/1/targets/0.description: Verteporfin PDT causes targeted choriocapillaris occlusion and remodeling of abnormal choroidal vessels, normalizing choroidal permeability and reducing subretinal fluid generation.

evidence.snippet: The VICI study found that oral eplerenone (25 mg/day for 1 week then increasing to 50 mg/day for up to 12 months) was not superior to placebo
evidence.explanation: The VICI randomized trial found oral eplerenone not superior to placebo (for improving visual acuity in chronic CSCR at 12 months), refuting the expectation of clinical benefit from mineralocorticoid receptor antagonism.

treatments/2.description: Eplerenone and spironolactone, oral mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists, were investigated as pharmacological treatments targeting the MR/cortisol pathway implicated in CSCR pathogenesis. The VICI randomized controlled trial (eplerenone vs. placebo in chronic CSCR) failed to meet its primary endpoint of improving best-corrected visual acuity at 12 months. Despite mechanistic rationale and early observational evidence, eplerenone did not demonstrate significant benefit over placebo for visual acuity in this pivotal trial. Routine use for chronic CSCR remains controversial; these agents may be considered when PDT is unavailable or contraindicated, but are not a substitute for PDT. Long-term RCT data are warranted before routine clinical adoption.

treatments/2/targets/0.description: MR antagonists block mineralocorticoid receptor signaling in choroidal endothelial cells, theoretically reducing vascular permeability; however, clinical benefit in BCVA was not demonstrated in the VICI RCT.

evidence.snippet: Available evidence supports half-dose (or half-fluence) verteporfin photodynamic therapy as the treatment of choice for CSC to reduce choroidal hyperpermeability.
evidence.explanation: 2025 expert review recommends PDT as the treatment of choice over micropulse laser, citing the PLACE trial results showing PDT superiority; micropulse is an acceptable but less effective alternative.

treatments/3.description: High-density subthreshold micropulse laser (577 nm HSML) delivers sub-lethal retinal laser energy to stimulate RPE function without causing visible burns. Complete SRF resolution rates range from 36–100% across studies. The PLACE randomized trial demonstrated that half-dose PDT was superior to high-density micropulse laser for chronic CSCR in SRF resolution rate and recurrence. Micropulse laser is a reasonable alternative when PDT is unavailable, contraindicated, or for extrafoveal leakage, but should not be preferred over PDT for chronic subfoveal CSCR.

treatments/3/targets/0.description: Subthreshold micropulse laser delivers sub-lethal thermal energy to the RPE, stimulating RPE cell function and reducing focal leakage without causing visible RPE burns or permanent tissue destruction.

evidence.snippet: We propose a step-wise chart for clinical decision-making in the management and treatment of CSC.
evidence.explanation: 2025 expert consensus includes focal laser photocoagulation as a treatment option for selected extrafoveal CSCR cases in its clinical decision-making algorithm.

treatments/4.description: Focal laser photocoagulation of the leakage point(s) identified on fluorescein angiography can accelerate SRF resolution in acute CSCR with extrafoveal focal leakage. Not appropriate for subfoveal or juxtafoveal leaks due to risk of causing permanent scotoma. Historical 5-year data suggest fewer recurrences and better VA than observation in some studies. Less commonly used since PDT has demonstrated superior outcomes for chronic and subfoveal CSCR.

treatments/4/targets/0.description: Focal laser photocoagulation creates a controlled thermal burn at the focal RPE leakage point identified on fluorescein angiography, sealing the defect and halting subretinal fluid transudation. Restricted to extrafoveal leaks to avoid central scotoma.

evidence.snippet: A subset of patients with chronic CSC can develop choroidal neovascularisation, and these patients should be treated with intravitreal anti-vascular endothelial growth factor agents.
evidence.explanation: 2025 expert consensus explicitly recommends anti-VEGF for chronic CSCR complicated by choroidal neovascularization, distinguishing this as a separate indication from PDT for non-neovascular CSCR.

treatments/5.description: Intravitreal anti-VEGF agents (bevacizumab, ranibizumab, aflibercept) are standard treatment specifically for CSCR complicated by active choroidal neovascularization (type 1 CNV). The MINERVA randomized trial supported anti-VEGF efficacy for CSC with macular neovascularization. Anti-VEGF is not effective as monotherapy for uncomplicated CSCR without CNV and meta-analyses have not confirmed efficacy in non-neovascular acute CSCR. One randomized study showed ranibizumab inferior to low-fluence PDT for anatomical outcomes in non-CNV CSCR.

open_questions/0.rationale: Current animal models recapitulate specific upstream mechanisms: aldosterone treatment in rats produces subretinal fluid and RPE changes consistent with mineralocorticoid receptor overstimulation, and choroidal congestion mouse models address some aspects of vascular hyperpermeability. However, no animal species possesses a pachychoroid anatomy (thickened choroid with enlarged Haller's layer vessels and attenuated choriocapillaris) homologous to the human lesion. The genetic risk architecture—particularly CFH pathway and PTPRB variants—is not modeled by any existing system. This mismatch limits translational inference: pharmacological effects shown in rodent models (e.g., melatonin preventing aldosterone-induced SRF in rats) may not reflect efficacy against the full human pachychoroid disease. Validating the PTPRB-VE-PTP and CFH mechanisms requires species with relevant choroidal anatomy or humanized vascular endothelial systems.

evidence.snippet: Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (HR HPV) is the necessary cause of cervical cancer.
evidence.explanation: States HPV persistence as the necessary cause of cervical cancer.

evidence.snippet: Integration of human papilloma virus (HPV) was observed in all HPV18-related samples and 76% of HPV16-related samples, and was associated with structural aberrations and increased target-gene expression.
evidence.explanation: TCGA confirmed near-universal HPV integration in HPV18-positive cervical cancers and frequent integration in HPV16-positive cancers, linked to host structural alterations and target-gene upregulation.

steps/1.description: Integration of HPV DNA into the host genome disrupts the viral E2 gene, which normally represses E6/E7 expression. This results in constitutive overexpression of E6 and E7 oncoproteins, a critical step in malignant progression from CIN3 to invasive carcinoma.

evidence.snippet: Integration of human papilloma virus (HPV) was observed in all HPV18-related samples and 76% of HPV16-related samples, and was associated with structural aberrations and increased target-gene expression.
evidence.explanation: Establishes that HPV integration is near-universal in HPV18-positive and frequent in HPV16-positive cervical tumors, the genomic precondition for loss of E2-mediated repression modeled here. Marked INDIRECT because the "target-gene expression" measured is that of host genes at integration sites, not E6/E7 transcript levels, which this quote does not report.

evidence.snippet: The E6 protein encoded by the oncogenic human papillomavirus types 16 and 18 is one of two viral products expressed in HPV-associated cancers.
evidence.explanation: This establishes E6 as an expressed viral oncoprotein in HPV-associated cancers.

steps/2.description: HPV integration-associated loss of viral regulatory control sustains expression of the E6 and E7 viral oncoproteins, feeding the p53 and pRB disruption arms of cervical carcinogenesis.

evidence.snippet: In this study we demonstrate that the E6 proteins of the oncogenic HPVs that bind p53 stimulate the degradation of p53.
evidence.explanation: Classic mechanistic evidence shows high-risk HPV E6 promotes p53 degradation, supporting p53 checkpoint loss as a central cervical cancer mechanism.

steps/3.description: The HPV E6 oncoprotein binds to the cellular E3 ubiquitin ligase E6AP and targets p53 for proteasomal degradation. Loss of p53 function eliminates DNA damage checkpoints, allows cells with genomic instability to survive, and prevents apoptosis of infected cells.

evidence.snippet: The E6-promoted degradation of p53 is ATP dependent and involves the ubiquitin-dependent protease system.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the proteolytic route by which E6 destroys p53, the direct cause of this node's checkpoint/DNA-damage-response failure. Marked INDIRECT because this 1990 biochemical study characterizes p53 destruction itself and does not measure the downstream DNA-damage response or checkpoint readout.

steps/4.description: E6-mediated degradation of p53 weakens DNA-damage checkpoint and apoptosis responses, allowing damaged cervical epithelial cells to survive instead of undergoing growth arrest or programmed cell death.

evidence.snippet: Integration of human papilloma virus (HPV) was observed in all HPV18-related samples and 76% of HPV16-related samples, and was associated with structural aberrations and increased target-gene expression.
evidence.explanation: Human cervical tumor genomic data link HPV integration with structural aberrations, supporting genomic instability in HPV-driven carcinogenesis.

steps/5.description: HPV integration and impaired checkpoint control are associated with structural genomic aberrations, supporting the accumulation of alterations that help drive malignant progression.

evidence.snippet: These assays have been used to demonstrate that the E7 oncoprotein of the human papilloma virus type-16 can form similar complexes with p105-RB.
evidence.explanation: Classic biochemical evidence shows HPV16 E7 binds the retinoblastoma gene product, supporting pRB-pathway inactivation.

steps/6.description: The HPV E7 oncoprotein binds to and inactivates the retinoblastoma protein (pRB), releasing E2F transcription factors to drive uncontrolled cell cycle progression. E7 also targets pRB family members p107 and p130, and destabilizes pRB through proteasomal degradation.

evidence.snippet: These results suggest that these three DNA viruses may utilize similar mechanisms in transformation and implicate RB binding as a possible step in human papilloma virus-associated carcinogenesis.
evidence.explanation: RB binding by HPV16 E7 implicates loss of RB-mediated cell-cycle restraint in HPV carcinogenesis. Marked INDIRECT because this binding study proposes RB binding as a possible transforming step rather than measuring S-phase entry or proliferation directly.

steps/7.description: E7 binding to pRB disrupts retinoblastoma-mediated cell-cycle restraint, enabling inappropriate S-phase entry and proliferation of HPV-transformed cervical epithelial cells.

evidence.snippet: Precursor lesions of the cervix persist longer and progress more quickly in women with oncogenic HPV infections than in women with non-oncogenic infections or without HPV.
evidence.explanation: A longitudinal HPV/CIN cohort supports oncogenic HPV-associated persistence and faster progression of cervical precursor lesions.

steps/8.description: HPV infection induces a spectrum of preinvasive lesions graded as CIN1, CIN2, and CIN3 (carcinoma in situ). Low-grade lesions (CIN1) often regress, while high-grade lesions (CIN2/3) have significant risk of progression to invasive carcinoma over 10-20 years if untreated.

evidence.snippet: Common symptoms were abnormal vaginal bleeding, low abdominal pain, and malodorous vaginal discharge reported among 75.8%, 66.4%, and 39.6% of cases, respectively.
evidence.explanation: Retrospective review of 149 cervical cancer patients in Botswana identifies abnormal vaginal bleeding as the most common presenting symptom (75.8%), supporting its classification as a frequent diagnostic phenotype.

steps/9.description: The most common presenting symptom, including postcoital bleeding, intermenstrual bleeding, or postmenopausal bleeding. Often the first sign of invasive disease.

evidence.snippet: Common symptoms were abnormal vaginal bleeding, low abdominal pain, and malodorous vaginal discharge reported among 75.8%, 66.4%, and 39.6% of cases, respectively.
evidence.explanation: Same Botswana retrospective review reports malodorous vaginal discharge in 39.6% of cervical cancer cases, supporting its classification as a frequent presenting symptom.

steps/10.description: Watery, mucoid, or blood-tinged vaginal discharge may occur, sometimes with foul odor in advanced cases due to tumor necrosis.

evidence.snippet: Common symptoms were abnormal vaginal bleeding, low abdominal pain, and malodorous vaginal discharge reported among 75.8%, 66.4%, and 39.6% of cases, respectively.
evidence.explanation: Low abdominal pain was reported in 66.4% of cervical cancer patients in this Botswana cohort, with the same study identifying low abdominal pain as a significant predictor of locally advanced disease at presentation.

steps/11.description: Pelvic pain typically indicates locally advanced disease with parametrial invasion, pelvic sidewall involvement, or nerve compression.

evidence.snippet: A total of 130 were patients included, 54 of which (41.5%) had hematuria.
evidence.explanation: Prospective study of 130 newly diagnosed cervical cancer patients quantifies hematuria prevalence (41.5%), with hematuria shown to be a sensitive screening test for urinary bladder mucosal infiltration in advanced cervical cancer, supporting classification as a frequent phenotype.

steps/12.description: Hematuria is a frequent urinary manifestation in advanced cervical cancer and may reflect bladder mucosal involvement.

edges/0.description: p53 degradation removes critical cell cycle checkpoints

edges/1.description: Cells with damaged DNA continue to proliferate

edges/2.description: Cells with unrepaired damage persist and acquire additional alterations

edges/3.description: Genomic alterations contribute to progression from preinvasive lesions

edges/4.description: E2F release drives S-phase entry independent of growth signals

edges/5.description: Persistent proliferative signaling contributes to preinvasive lesion progression

edges/6.description: Loss of E2 repression leads to unchecked oncoprotein production

edges/7.description: Sustained E6 expression drives p53 degradation

edges/8.description: Sustained E7 expression drives pRB inactivation

edges/9.description: Progressive cervical neoplasia and invasive tumor disrupt cervical mucosa and vessels, causing abnormal bleeding.

edges/10.description: Progressive cervical tumor growth and necrosis contribute to abnormal vaginal discharge.

edges/11.description: Locally advanced cervical tumor growth can involve parametrial or pelvic tissues and cause pelvic pain.

edges/12.description: Advanced local tumor extension can involve the bladder mucosa and produce hematuria.

evidence.snippet: Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (HR HPV) is the necessary cause of cervical cancer.
evidence.explanation: Supports treating persistent HPV infection as the initiating exposure acting on the E6-mediated mechanism curated here.

edges/13.description: Infection of the cervical epithelium is what brings the E6 oncoprotein into the cell, so the exposure initiates the earliest curated mechanism.

genes/0.notes: Rather than somatic mutation, p53 function is lost through E6-mediated degradation in HPV-positive cervical cancer. Rare HPV-negative cervical cancers may harbor TP53 mutations.

genes/1.notes: PIK3CA mutations occur in approximately 25-35% of cervical cancers, activating PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling. May represent a therapeutic target.

treatments/0.description: Prophylactic vaccination against HPV-16, 18, and other high-risk types prevents infection and subsequent development of cervical cancer and precancerous lesions. Most effective when administered before sexual debut.

treatments/1.description: Loop electrosurgical excision procedure (LEEP) or cold knife cone biopsy for treatment of high-grade cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN2/3). Allows fertility preservation while treating preinvasive disease.

treatments/2.description: Surgical treatment for early-stage invasive cervical cancer (IA2-IB2) includes removal of the uterus, parametria, and upper vagina, with pelvic lymphadenectomy. Fertility-sparing radical trachelectomy may be considered in select cases.

treatments/3.description: Concurrent cisplatin-based chemotherapy with external beam radiation and brachytherapy is the standard treatment for locally advanced cervical cancer (stages IB3-IVA). Improves survival compared to radiation alone.

evidence.snippet: leading to regulatory approval of pembrolizumab for persistent, recurrent, or metastatic CC tumors expressing PD-L1 with a combined positive score (CPS) ≥ 1
evidence.explanation: The 2023 SEOM-GEICO cervical cancer guideline states the approved pembrolizumab indication this entry describes: persistent, recurrent, or metastatic disease with PD-L1 CPS of at least 1. Replaces a previously quoted sentence that referred only to "immunotherapy" generically without naming pembrolizumab.

treatments/4.description: PD-1 inhibitor approved for recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer with PD-L1 expression (CPS score of at least 1) in combination with chemotherapy, or as monotherapy in previously treated PD-L1 positive tumors.

evidence.snippet: Using mice deficient in major innate immunity signaling components, we found that signaling through the mitochondrial antiviral-signaling protein (MAVS) is required for viral clearance from the heart
evidence.explanation: Establishes MAVS-dependent sensing as the innate signalling step whose loss prevents cardiac viral clearance, and states that the deficiency is a property of the mouse rather than an effect of the infection.

steps/0.description: Loss of signalling through the mitochondrial antiviral-signaling protein MAVS, the adaptor for cytoplasmic viral RNA sensing. In the model system this state is produced genetically rather than by the virus, which is why it is curated as an upstream host lesion with no incoming edge from infection: the reviewer-suggested route from cardiac infection to sensing failure is not something the source shows. What the source does show is the consequence — mice deficient in MAVS signalling fail to clear chikungunya virus from the heart — so the outgoing edge, not an incoming one, is where the evidence sits. PROVISIONAL because no comparable sensing lesion has been demonstrated in patients with chikungunya cardiac disease.

evidence.snippet: CHIKV primarily targets muscle, joint, and skin fibroblasts, a cell and tissue tropism similar to that observed in biopsy samples of CHIKV-infected humans
evidence.explanation: Identifies the fibroblast as the predominant target cell and states that the mouse tropism matches human biopsy material, which is what licenses using this node as the root for both arms.

steps/1.description: Chikungunya virus establishes productive replication preferentially in fibroblasts of muscle, joint and skin, a tropism recovered from human biopsy material as well as from the mouse model. This node is the shared root of the entry: the musculoskeletal syndrome and the cardiac arm both begin from infection of the same cell lineage in different tissues.

evidence.snippet: we demonstrate that CHIKV directly infects and actively replicates in cardiac fibroblasts
evidence.explanation: Establishes the cardiac fibroblast as a genuine replication site, using both an immunocompetent mouse model and human primary cardiac cells.

steps/2.description: Chikungunya virus directly infects and actively replicates in cardiac fibroblasts. This is shown in an immunocompetent mouse model and in primary human cardiac cells, so the cardiac arm rests on a demonstrated cell target rather than on the clinical association alone.

evidence.snippet: We found that CHIKV infection induced IL-17A production in the heart
evidence.explanation: The only source that localises IL-17A production to cardiac tissue, and the reason this node is marked PROVISIONAL.

evidence.snippet: Sera from CHIKV-infected patients who displayed both acute and chronic disease showed high levels of IL-17, IL-6, IL-21, IL-22, and IL-23, especially during the chronic phase of disease
evidence.explanation: PARTIAL because it establishes that IL-17 rises in infected patients, which is the observation this node starts from, but measures serum and so cannot place the cytokine in the heart.

steps/3.description: IL-17A is produced locally in chikungunya-infected cardiac tissue. PROVISIONAL because the cardiac localisation rests solely on a preprint: the peer-reviewed human data measure IL-17 in patient sera and the peer-reviewed mouse data measure it in joint and muscle, so neither places the cytokine in the heart.

evidence.snippet: Genetic deletion of IL-17A signaling significantly enhanced type I interferon responses and decreased viral burden in mouse hearts
evidence.explanation: Loss of signalling through this axis changes both interferon output and viral burden in cardiac tissue, which is what makes it a node rather than a bystander observation.

evidence.snippet: blockade of IL-17RA with an FDA-approved monoclonal antibody for plaque psoriasis, Brodalumab, drastically increased type I interferon production and reduced viral replication in both human cardiac fibroblasts and human embryonic kidney 293 (HEK 293) cells
evidence.explanation: Pharmacological confirmation in human cardiac fibroblasts that the receptor, specifically, carries the effect.

steps/4.description: IL-17A signalling through IL-17RA in cardiac tissue. Removing the receptor or blocking it pharmacologically raises the local interferon response and lowers viral burden, so this is the step the emerging hypothesis places upstream of the interferon response rather than downstream of the damage. PROVISIONAL because every result placing IL-17RA signalling in the heart comes from the same preprint.

evidence.snippet: In immunocompetent mice, CHIKV is cleared from cardiac tissue without significant damage through the induction of a local type I interferon response from both infected and non-infected cardiac cells
evidence.explanation: Establishes that the local interferon response is what normally prevents cardiac damage, which is what makes its restraint pathogenic.

evidence.snippet: Genetic deletion of IL-17A signaling significantly enhanced type I interferon responses and decreased viral burden in mouse hearts
evidence.explanation: Read in reverse, intact IL-17A signalling holds the interferon response below the level the deletion reveals.

steps/5.description: Clearance of chikungunya virus from the heart depends on a local type I interferon response raised by both infected and uninfected cardiac cells. Anything that blunts that response therefore converts a self-limiting cardiac infection into a persistent one. Two routes to a blunted response reach this node and they differ sharply in standing: loss of MAVS-dependent innate sensing is a peer-reviewed genetic result and has its own upstream node, whereas restraint by IL-17RA signalling is the emerging claim and is marked as such on its incoming edge. The node is PROVISIONAL because interferon insufficiency has not been measured in the hearts of infected humans.

evidence.snippet: Large vessel vasculitis was observed for up to 60 days post infection, suggesting CHIKV can lead to vascular inflammation and potential long-lasting cardiovascular complications
evidence.explanation: Quantifies how long the consequences of failed clearance persist in the model, and is the authors' own hedged extrapolation to humans.

steps/6.description: Virus that is not cleared continues to replicate in the myocardium and in the vascular tissue at the base of the heart. In the mouse this persistence is prolonged, with large vessel vasculitis still present two months after infection. Whether human cardiac involvement reflects persistence or a single acute insult has not been established, hence PROVISIONAL.

evidence.snippet: In the absence of MAVS signaling, persistent infection leads to focal myocarditis and vasculitis of the large vessels attached to the base of the heart
evidence.explanation: Names the two lesions that constitute this node in the model system.

evidence.snippet: reduced immune cell infiltration into cardiac tissue, and mitigated cardiac injury
evidence.explanation: Interrupting IL-17A signalling removes the infiltrate and the injury, placing this node downstream of the IL-17A arm.

evidence.snippet: Cardiovascular manifestations can be considered common and have been reported in France, India, Sri Lanka, Malaysia, Colombia, Venezuela and USA
evidence.explanation: PARTIAL because the systematic review establishes that cardiac involvement occurs in infected patients but reports no mechanism, and its own methods section notes that isolated cardiac compromise is not common.

steps/7.description: Inflammatory cell infiltration of cardiac tissue with focal myocarditis and vasculitis of the great vessels at the base of the heart. Blocking IL-17A signalling reduces the pro-inflammatory mediators, the infiltrate and the injury together, which is the observation that makes this node the endpoint of the IL-17A arm rather than an independent process.

evidence.snippet: CHIKV-infected mice lacking IL-17A showed reduced tissue inflammation and neutrophil infiltration, compared to wild-type mice
evidence.explanation: The genetic result defining both the composition of the infiltrate and its dependence on IL-17A.

evidence.snippet: These investigations showed a role for IL-17 in the acute phase of CHIKV infection and also during the postacute disease resolution phase
evidence.explanation: Extends the requirement beyond the acute phase, which matters because the human cytokine signal is strongest in chronic disease.

steps/8.description: Inflammatory infiltration of joint and muscle tissue, with neutrophils prominent, underlying the arthralgia and myalgia of acute chikungunya and persisting into the postacute phase. IL-17A is required for it in the mouse and is elevated in patients, most strongly during chronic disease; that dependence is recorded as evidence on this node rather than as an edge from the cardiac IL-17A nodes, because the peer-reviewed result is about joint and muscle tissue and the cardiac nodes are explicitly localised to the heart.

evidence.snippet: The disease typically consists of an acute illness characterised by fever, rash, and incapacitating arthralgia.
evidence.explanation: Fever is a typical feature of acute chikungunya.

evidence.snippet: The disease typically consists of an acute illness characterised by fever, rash, and incapacitating arthralgia.
evidence.explanation: Rash is a typical feature of acute chikungunya.

evidence.snippet: The disease typically consists of an acute illness characterised by fever, rash, and incapacitating arthralgia.
evidence.explanation: Arthralgia is a hallmark of acute chikungunya.

evidence.snippet: Cardiovascular manifestations can be considered common and have been reported in France, India, Sri Lanka, Malaysia, Colombia, Venezuela and USA, including mainly, but no limited to: hypotension, shock and circulatory collapse, Raynaud phenomenon, arrhythmias, murmurs, myocarditis, dilated cardiomyopathy, congestive insufficiency, heart failure and altered function profile (Troponins, CPK).
evidence.explanation: Systematic review of 40 reports listing myocarditis among the cardiovascular manifestations observed in patients with chikungunya.

steps/12.description: Myocardial inflammation reported among the cardiovascular manifestations of systemic chikungunya virus infection, alongside arrhythmias, dilated cardiomyopathy and heart failure. No frequency band is asserted: the source that establishes these manifestations occur also states that isolated cardiac compromise is uncommon, and the two statements cannot be reconciled into a band without going beyond what is reported.

edges/0.description: The same fibroblast tropism extends to the resident fibroblast population of the myocardium.

edges/1.description: Acute systemic CHIKV infection produces fever.

edges/2.description: Acute systemic CHIKV infection produces rash.

edges/3.description: Infection of joint and muscle fibroblasts is the substrate for the arthralgia and myalgia that define acute chikungunya.

evidence.snippet: We found that CHIKV infection induced IL-17A production in the heart
evidence.explanation: Places IL-17A downstream of cardiac infection rather than as a pre-existing host state.

edges/4.description: Cardiac infection is itself the stimulus for local IL-17A production.

evidence.snippet: In the absence of MAVS signaling, persistent infection leads to focal myocarditis and vasculitis of the large vessels attached to the base of the heart
evidence.explanation: The loss-of-function result: without MAVS signalling the interferon response no longer clears the virus and cardiac disease follows.

edges/5.description: The peer-reviewed route to a cardiac interferon response too weak to clear the virus, and the counterpart of the emerging IL-17A route into the same node.

evidence.snippet: blockade of IL-17RA with an FDA-approved monoclonal antibody for plaque psoriasis, Brodalumab, drastically increased type I interferon production and reduced viral replication in both human cardiac fibroblasts and human embryonic kidney 293 (HEK 293) cells
evidence.explanation: Blocking the receptor reverses the effect of the ligand, which is what types this as a ligand-to-receptor-signalling edge rather than an assumed one.

edges/6.description: Locally produced IL-17A acts on cardiac cells through its receptor IL-17RA, which is the step receptor blockade interrupts.

evidence.snippet: Genetic deletion of IL-17A signaling significantly enhanced type I interferon responses and decreased viral burden in mouse hearts
evidence.explanation: A loss-of-function result in the direction the hypothesis predicts, and the strongest single statement of the causal claim.

edges/7.description: The edge that carries the emerging claim: IL-17RA signalling suppresses the local interferon response rather than merely accompanying it.

evidence.snippet: In the absence of MAVS signaling, persistent infection leads to focal myocarditis and vasculitis of the large vessels attached to the base of the heart
evidence.explanation: Directly links failed innate antiviral signalling to persistence in the heart.

edges/8.description: An interferon response insufficient to clear the virus leaves replicating virus in cardiac tissue.

edges/9.description: Persistent replication in cardiac tissue recruits the infiltrate that produces the myocardial lesion.

evidence.snippet: Cardiovascular manifestations can be considered common and have been reported in France, India, Sri Lanka, Malaysia, Colombia, Venezuela and USA, including mainly, but no limited to: hypotension, shock and circulatory collapse, Raynaud phenomenon, arrhythmias, murmurs, myocarditis, dilated cardiomyopathy, congestive insufficiency, heart failure and altered function profile (Troponins, CPK).
evidence.explanation: Names myocarditis among the cardiovascular manifestations observed in infected patients, which is the clinical expression of this node.

edges/10.description: The tissue lesion presenting clinically. Myocarditis is the phenotype the myocardial inflammation and injury node produces, and is named as such both in the mouse histology and in the patient literature.

evidence.snippet: Up to 40% of patients experience persistent joint inflammation and arthralgia, which can persist for months or years after infection
evidence.explanation: States joint inflammation and arthralgia together in patients, which is what links this tissue node to the phenotype.

edges/11.description: Persistent inflammation of the joint is what patients experience as the arthralgia that defines chikungunya and that outlasts the acute illness.

evidence.snippet: Treatment of acute CHIK is symptomatic
evidence.explanation: The abstract notes that acute chikungunya treatment is symptomatic.

treatments/0.description: Supportive care for acute chikungunya.

evidence.snippet: we demonstrate that IL-17A signaling facilitates CHIKV replication via suppressing antiviral type I interferon responses
evidence.explanation: States the hypothesis in the direction that defines this group, that IL-17A acts upstream of the interferon response rather than downstream of the damage.

evidence.snippet: Sera from CHIKV-infected patients who displayed both acute and chronic disease showed high levels of IL-17, IL-6, IL-21, IL-22, and IL-23, especially during the chronic phase of disease
evidence.explanation: PARTIAL because it establishes that IL-17 is elevated in infected patients, which is the observation the hypothesis starts from, but says nothing about interferon or about the heart.

hypotheses/0.description: Under this model the IL-17A that chikungunya virus infection induces in the heart is not merely a marker of inflammation but an active brake on the antiviral response: IL-17A acting through IL-17RA suppresses local type I interferon production, so viral clearance from cardiac tissue is slowed and the resulting viral burden drives myocardial inflammation and injury. The prediction that distinguishes it from a bystander account is directional and testable, and has been tested only in a preprint so far: removing IL-17A signalling should raise interferon output and lower viral burden rather than simply lowering inflammation. Genetic deletion of Il17a or Il17ra and antibody blockade of IL-17RA both do exactly that in mouse hearts and in primary human cardiac fibroblasts. The status is EMERGING rather than CANONICAL because the only source making the interferon claim is not peer reviewed, and because the peer-reviewed human data show elevated circulating IL-17 in patients without establishing its direction of effect on interferon or on the heart.

evidence.snippet: Using a novel heterozygous interferon receptor-deficient mouse model
evidence.explanation: The authors' own statement of the animal system used, which is what makes the mismatch explicit: the interferon claim is made in a host with an engineered interferon receptor deficiency.

evidence.snippet: blockade of IL-17RA with an FDA-approved monoclonal antibody for plaque psoriasis, Brodalumab, drastically increased type I interferon production and reduced viral replication in both human cardiac fibroblasts and human embryonic kidney 293 (HEK 293) cells
evidence.explanation: PARTIAL, and split out from the mouse item because it is the human arm of the same study and a different evidence type: primary human cardiac fibroblast and HEK 293 culture supplies the right species and cell type but no immune compartment, vasculature or chronic timescale.

open_questions/0.rationale: The mismatch here is unusually pointed, because the model system is compromised in precisely the axis the hypothesis is about. The directional claim rests on a heterozygous interferon alpha, beta and gamma receptor-deficient mouse, so the interferon response being measured is already operating at reduced receptor dosage; whether the same restraint would be visible, or would matter, in a fully interferon-competent host is not established. The human arm of the same source is primary cardiac fibroblast culture, which supplies the correct species and cell type but no immune compartment, no vasculature and no chronic timescale. On the peer-reviewed side there is a clean separation of what is known: elevated IL-17 in patient sera, and IL-17A dependence of joint and muscle inflammation in mice, neither of which speaks to interferon or to the heart. Note also that the source is a preprint and has not been peer reviewed, so the usual caution about a single unreviewed result applies on top of the model question.

evidence.snippet: blockade of IL-17RA with an FDA-approved monoclonal antibody for plaque psoriasis, Brodalumab, drastically increased type I interferon production and reduced viral replication in both human cardiac fibroblasts and human embryonic kidney 293 (HEK 293) cells
evidence.explanation: The whole of the pharmacological evidence, and it is cell culture in human cardiac fibroblasts and a kidney cell line rather than any clinical observation.

evidence.snippet: Cardiac compromise is not so common in isolated episodes
evidence.explanation: PARTIAL, and included because it bears on feasibility rather than on mechanism: the target population for a cardiac endpoint trial is a minority of infected patients, which is part of why no such study exists.

open_questions/1.rationale: Brodalumab is an approved IL-17RA antagonist for plaque psoriasis, and the preprint reports that it raises interferon production and lowers viral replication in human cardiac fibroblasts and in HEK 293 cells, including when given after infection. That is a mechanistically coherent repurposing proposal and nothing more: there is no clinical study in chikungunya, no human safety or dosing data in acute arboviral infection, and the intervention is immunosuppressive in a setting where IL-17 also contributes to control of infection. This entry therefore deliberately carries no treatment record for IL-17RA blockade and records the proposal here instead, so that a future curator can see that the omission was a decision rather than an oversight. The bar for promoting it to a treatment with a target_mechanisms edge is a clinical study in infected patients, not a stronger preclinical result.

evidence.snippet: Pediatric CPTs lack recurrent driver alterations except for TP53, whereas CPTs in adults show TERT promoter mutations or a novel CCDC47-PRKCA gene fusion, being associated with a more unfavorable clinical course.
evidence.explanation: Establishes TP53 as the only recurrent driver lesion in pediatric choroid plexus tumors.

evidence.snippet: TP53 mutations were found in 50% of choroid plexus carcinomas (CPCs).
evidence.explanation: Quantifies the frequency of somatic TP53 mutation in carcinoma.

evidence.snippet: Additionally, two sequence variants known to confer TP53 dysfunction, TP53 codon72 and MDM2 SNP309, coexisted in the majority of TP53 wild-type CPCs (92%) and not in TP53 mutated CPC (P = .04), which suggests a complementary mechanism of TP53 dysfunction in the absence of a TP53 mutation.
evidence.explanation: Supports p53 dysfunction arising without a TP53 mutation via modifier variants.

steps/3.description: Loss of p53 tumor-suppressor function - by germline pathogenic TP53 variant (Li-Fraumeni syndrome) with somatic loss of the remaining allele, by somatic TP53 mutation, or by the combination of TP53 codon 72 and MDM2 SNP309 variants that confer p53 dysfunction in the absence of a mutation - is the only recurrent driver lesion in pediatric choroid plexus tumors. It is concentrated in carcinoma, where roughly half of tumors carry a TP53 mutation, and is absent or rare in papilloma.

evidence.snippet: Copy-number alterations mainly represented whole-chromosomal alterations with subgroup-specific enrichments
evidence.explanation: Establishes whole-chromosome copy-number change as the dominant genomic alteration class and its subgroup specificity.

evidence.snippet: Recurrent copy number losses of chromosomes 5, 6, 16, 18, 19, and 22 as well as gains of chromosomes 1, 2, 4, 12, and 20 were identified.
evidence.explanation: Enumerates the recurrent whole-chromosome imbalances in carcinoma.

evidence.snippet: Allele-specific CN analysis of CPCs revealed two novel subgroups according to DNA content: hypodiploid and hyperdiploid CPCs.
evidence.explanation: Supports genome-wide ploidy disturbance as a defining feature of carcinoma.

evidence.snippet: Mutually exclusive TP53 and EPHA7 point mutations, coupled with the amplification of chromosome 1, were exclusively identified in CPC. In contrast, amplification of chromosome 9 was specific to CPP.
evidence.explanation: Identifies the copy-number and point-mutation events that discriminate carcinoma from papilloma, including the mutually exclusive TP53/EPHA7 pattern.

evidence.snippet: gains of Chr1, 2 and 21q in "pediatric B" and gains of Chr5 and 9 and loss of Chr21q in "adult"
evidence.explanation: The subgroup-specific whole-chromosome enrichments that define the copy-number classes.

evidence.snippet: methylation profiling unveiled hypomethylation in major repeat regions, including long interspersed nuclear elements, short interspersed nuclear elements, long terminal repeats, and retrotransposons in CPC compared to CPP, implying that the loss of epigenetic silencing of transposable elements may play a role in tumorigenesis of CPC
evidence.explanation: Adds the epigenetic arm - loss of transposable-element silencing - as a candidate contributor to the carcinoma genomic state.

steps/4.description: Choroid plexus tumors are characterised by whole-chromosome copy-number alterations rather than focal driver events. Recurrent gains and losses partition the family into methylation/copy-number subgroups and vary with patient age; carcinomas show complex, hyperdiploid or hypodiploid genomes, and a greater burden of mutant TP53 copies tracks with a more aggressive course.

evidence.snippet: On the contrary, TERT promoter mutations were encountered in 7/28 adult patients (25%) and associated with shorter progression-free survival (log-rank test, p=0.015).
evidence.explanation: Establishes the frequency, adult restriction and prognostic effect of TERT promoter mutation.

evidence.snippet: Pediatric CPTs lack recurrent driver alterations except for TP53, whereas CPTs in adults show TERT promoter mutations or a novel CCDC47-PRKCA gene fusion, being associated with a more unfavorable clinical course.
evidence.explanation: Contrasts the adult TERT/fusion route with the pediatric TP53 route.

evidence.snippet: ALT was highly enriched in primitive neuroectodermal tumors (12 %), choroid plexus carcinomas (23 %) and high-grade gliomas (22 %).
evidence.explanation: Documents the telomerase-independent alternative-lengthening-of-telomeres route to telomere maintenance in choroid plexus carcinoma, the pediatric counterpart of the adult TERT-promoter route this node models.

evidence.snippet: Somatic but not germline TP53 mutations were highly associated with ALT
evidence.explanation: Ties the alternative-lengthening route specifically to somatic TP53 mutation, distinguishing it from the germline predisposition arm.

steps/5.description: A separate, adult-restricted route into the same tumor. TERT promoter mutations occur in a quarter of adult choroid plexus tumor patients, reactivating telomerase and conferring replicative capacity; they are essentially absent from the pediatric-dominant subgroups, where TP53 is the recurrent lesion instead. TERT promoter mutation is prognostic in adults, associating with shorter progression-free survival, and a rare CCDC47-PRKCA fusion is a further adult-specific alteration reported in an aggressive papilloma. The pediatric counterpart of this telomere-maintenance requirement is telomerase-independent: alternative lengthening of telomeres is enriched in choroid plexus carcinoma (23% of cases) and is tied to somatic, not germline, TP53 mutation.

evidence.snippet: In contrast to MCCs in the CP epithelia, CPCs in humans are characterized by solitary cilia, frequent TP53 mutations, and disturbances to multiciliogenesis program directed by the GMNC-MCIDAS transcriptional network.
evidence.explanation: Human tumor observation of the loss of multiciliation and the associated transcriptional program.

evidence.snippet: NOTCH-driven CP tumors are monociliated, and disruption of the NOTCH complex restores multiciliation and decreases tumor growth.
evidence.explanation: Mouse experiment establishing that restoring multiciliation reduces tumor growth, supporting causality rather than correlation.

steps/6.description: Normal choroid plexus epithelium is multiciliated. Human choroid plexus carcinomas instead carry solitary cilia, reflecting failure of the GMNC-MCIDAS transcriptional program that specifies multiciliated cell fate. In mice, NOTCH activation suppresses GMNC/MCIDAS and generates monociliated choroid plexus tumors, while disrupting the NOTCH complex restores multiciliation and reduces tumor growth - identifying loss of terminal multiciliated differentiation as a permissive step rather than a bystander finding. In mice the defect is itself downstream of tumour-suppressor loss - carcinoma driven by combined Trp53 and Rb1 deletion shows GMNC-MCIDAS-attributable multiciliation defects - so this node is modelled as a consequence of the TP53 arm rather than an independent trigger. This arm rests principally on model-system evidence.

evidence.snippet: Choroid plexus tumors (CPTs) are intraventricular tumors derived from the choroid plexus epithelium and occur frequently in children.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the choroid plexus epithelium as the cell of origin for the whole family.

evidence.snippet: Expression of inward rectifier potassium channel Kir7.1 was confirmed in normal choroid plexus (34 of 35), choroid plexus papilloma (12 of 18), and choroid plexus carcinoma (5 of 5) but was not found in 100 other primary brain tumors and cerebral metastases.
evidence.explanation: Demonstrates retained choroid plexus epithelial identity in the neoplastic cells.

evidence.snippet: Here, we examine the heterogeneity of human choroid plexus tumors by single-nucleus transcriptome analysis of 23,906 cells from four disease-free choroid plexus and eleven choroid plexus tumors.
evidence.explanation: The single-nucleus atlas that resolves the tumor into its epithelial and stromal compartments.

evidence.snippet: We further characterize tumor type-specific stromal microenvironments that include altered macrophage and mesenchymal cell states, as well as changes in extracellular matrix components.
evidence.explanation: Establishes that the neoplastic epithelium sits in a tumor-type-specific stromal microenvironment with altered macrophage and mesenchymal states - the non-epithelial compartment of this node.

steps/7.description: Clonal expansion of transformed choroid plexus epithelial cells is the shared cellular event across all three graded entities. The proliferating cells retain choroid plexus epithelial identity - reliably demonstrable by Kir7.1 and stanniocalcin-1 immunoreactivity - and, critically for the disease mechanism, retain their secretory phenotype.

evidence.snippet: Choroid plexus papillomas are more common in the infratentorial compartment in adults and the supratentorial compartment in children.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the age-dependent anatomical distribution (fourth ventricle in adults, lateral ventricle in children).

evidence.snippet: Although generally found within the ventricular system, they can arise ectopically in the brain parenchyma or disseminate throughout the neuraxis.
evidence.explanation: Confirms the predominantly intraventricular location while noting ectopic and disseminated presentations.

steps/8.description: The tumor grows as an intraventricular papillary mass - lateral ventricle in children, fourth ventricle in adults - occupying the cerebrospinal fluid space. This single anatomical fact generates the two mechanistically distinct routes to hydrocephalus modelled downstream: the mass is itself secretory (overproduction) and it physically occupies and obstructs the cerebrospinal fluid pathway (obstruction).

evidence.snippet: Utilizing a ventricular perfusion technique, the rate of CSF formation was determined in a 2-year-old child before and after removal of a 74 g choroid plexus papilloma from the left lateral ventricle.
evidence.explanation: Describes the direct measurement establishing tumor-driven cerebrospinal fluid overproduction.

evidence.snippet: Patients with choroid plexus papillomas often present with communicating hydrocephalus secondary to cerebrospinal fluid overproduction.
evidence.explanation: Supports overproduction as a routine clinical presentation mechanism and its communicating character.

evidence.snippet: The CP secretes cerebrospinal fluid that circulates within the ventricular system, driven by ependymal cilia movement.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the normal secretory function of the tissue of origin that the tumor retains.

steps/9.description: The first of the two hydrocephalus mechanisms. Neoplastic choroid plexus epithelium continues to secrete cerebrospinal fluid, and a large tumor can raise the formation rate several-fold above normal. Ventricular perfusion measurement in a child with a 74 g lateral-ventricular papilloma showed a preoperative formation rate of 1.05 ml/min falling fivefold to 0.20 ml/min after resection. Because production outstrips absorptive capacity while the pathways themselves remain patent, this route classically produces a communicating hydrocephalus.

evidence.snippet: Dynamics of the cerebrospinal fluid were measured pre- and postoperatively in a patient with a choroid plexus papilloma associated with hydrocephalus. The production rate was 0.35 ml/min, absorption 0.0057 ml/min H2O, and the critical opening pressure 196 mm H2O.
evidence.explanation: Documents the measurement showing a normal production rate, isolating obstruction as the operative mechanism in that patient.

evidence.snippet: The persisting hydrocephalus is probably caused by an increase of the CSF outflow resistance because of a distal CSF-pathway obstruction.
evidence.explanation: Supports an outflow-resistance obstruction component that persists after the secretory tumor has been removed.

evidence.snippet: In spite of radical tumour removal, three years after the operation the axial computer tomography revealed a persistent hydrocephalus, but no recurrence of tumour.
evidence.explanation: Clinical demonstration that hydrocephalus can outlast removal of the overproducing tumour, requiring an obstruction/absorption mechanism.

steps/10.description: The second of the two hydrocephalus mechanisms, and independent of the first. The intraventricular mass can occlude the ventricular outflow route directly - for example a fourth-ventricular tumor blocking the outlets - producing hydrocephalus with a normal cerebrospinal fluid formation rate. In addition, obstruction of the subarachnoid pathways and increased cerebrospinal fluid outflow resistance, attributed to repeated subarachnoid bleeding from these highly vascular tumors and to raised cerebrospinal fluid protein, can persist after complete tumor removal, which is why some patients remain shunt-dependent despite radical resection and no residual tumor.

evidence.snippet: Differential gene expression analysis uncovered a significant overexpression of genes related to cell cycle regulation and epithelial-mesenchymal transition pathways in CPC compared to CPP.
evidence.explanation: Molecular characterisation of the papilloma-to-carcinoma difference.

evidence.snippet: However, two patients experienced a transition from a choroid plexus papilloma (WHO Grade I) and an atypical choroid plexus papilloma (WHO Grade II) to choroid plexus carcinomas (WHO Grade III).
evidence.explanation: Documents that grade progression to carcinoma occurs, albeit rarely.

steps/11.description: In a minority of tumors the epithelium acquires frank malignant features - hypercellularity, loss of the papillary architecture, brisk mitotic activity, pleomorphism and necrosis - defining WHO grade 3 carcinoma. This may be present de novo or, uncommonly, arise by documented progression from a previously resected grade 1 or grade 2 lesion. Carcinoma is transcriptionally distinguished from papilloma by upregulated cell-cycle and epithelial-mesenchymal transition programs.

evidence.snippet: Metastases were present at diagnosis in 17% of APP patients, 5% of CPP patients, and 21% of CPC patients.
evidence.explanation: Grade-stratified frequency of dissemination at diagnosis across the family.

evidence.snippet: Although generally found within the ventricular system, they can arise ectopically in the brain parenchyma or disseminate throughout the neuraxis.
evidence.explanation: Confirms that even grade 1 papilloma can disseminate through the cerebrospinal fluid pathways.

steps/12.description: Invasion of adjacent brain parenchyma and seeding of the cerebrospinal fluid pathways is the principal route to treatment failure. Metastatic disease is present at diagnosis in about a fifth of carcinomas and a sixth of atypical papillomas, and even papilloma can occasionally disseminate through the neuraxis.

evidence.snippet: Patients with choroid plexus papillomas often present with communicating hydrocephalus secondary to cerebrospinal fluid overproduction.
evidence.explanation: Establishes hydrocephalus as the dominant clinical presentation of choroid plexus tumors.

steps/13.description: The convergent consequence of both hydrocephalus mechanisms. Ventricular dilatation and raised intracranial pressure produce the characteristic clinical syndrome, which differs by age: in infants with open sutures, macrocephaly and a bulging fontanelle; in older children and adults, headache, vomiting and papilledema. Posterior-fossa (fourth-ventricular) tumors additionally produce cerebellar signs.

evidence.snippet: Patients with choroid plexus papillomas often present with communicating hydrocephalus secondary to cerebrospinal fluid overproduction.
evidence.explanation: Supports hydrocephalus as the characteristic presentation and names the overproduction route.

evidence.snippet: The hydrocephalus was due solely to obstruction of the fourth ventricle.
evidence.explanation: Supports the obstructive route as an independent cause of the same phenotype.

evidence.snippet: Hydrocephalus is the most common presentation of choroid plexus tumors; it is thought to be caused either by mass effect obstructing the cerebrospinal fluid pathways or secretory properties of the tumor.
evidence.explanation: States the dual mechanism explicitly - obstruction by mass effect OR secretory overproduction - which is why this entry models them as two nodes.

steps/14.description: The dominant presenting feature across the family. It arises by two distinct routes - cerebrospinal fluid overproduction by the secretory tumor epithelium (classically communicating) and obstruction of the cerebrospinal fluid pathways by mass effect - and both may operate in the same patient.

evidence.snippet: Whereas these data are regarded as conclusive evidence of CSF overproduction by a choroid plexus papilloma, the pathogenesis of generalized ventricular enlargement in this case was due to part to obstruction of the subarachnoid pathways.
evidence.explanation: Documents the generalized ventricular enlargement from which raised intracranial pressure follows; the abstract does not report a pressure measurement, so support is partial.

evidence.snippet: He was found to have an enlarged head circumference, a full and tense fontanel, splayed sutures, and forced downward gaze.
evidence.explanation: The classical infant sign cluster of raised intracranial pressure - head expansion, tense fontanelle, sutural diastasis and the setting-sun sign - in a child with a choroid plexus papilloma.

steps/15.description: Expansion of the cerebrospinal fluid compartment raises intracranial pressure, which drives the headache, vomiting, papilledema and (in infants) fontanelle and head-circumference signs.

evidence.snippet: This child presented with macrocephaly, irritability, inability to roll over, and vomiting.
evidence.explanation: Macrocephaly as a documented presenting sign of a third-ventricular choroid plexus papilloma in a 3-month-old.

evidence.snippet: Incidence was highest among children less than one year old among all subtypes (CPP AAIR: 0.278; aCPP AAIR: 0.140; CPC AAIR: 0.195), reducing as patients aged.
evidence.explanation: Supports the infantile age distribution that makes macrocephaly a characteristic sign; the abstract does not itself enumerate presenting signs.

steps/16.description: In infants with unfused cranial sutures, chronic hydrocephalus expands the calvarium and produces an abnormally large head circumference. Because the incidence peak is in the first year of life, this is a common mode of presentation.

evidence.snippet: Case 1: a 2-month-old baby girl presented with bulging fontanelle, sunsetting eyes.
evidence.explanation: Bulging fontanelle as the documented presenting sign of a third-ventricular choroid plexus tumor in a 2-month-old.

evidence.snippet: He was found to have an enlarged head circumference, a full and tense fontanel, splayed sutures, and forced downward gaze.
evidence.explanation: A second case documenting the tense/full fontanelle in an infant with a choroid plexus papilloma.

steps/17.description: Outward bowing of the unfused anterior fontanelle is a direct infant sign of raised intracranial pressure from tumor-associated hydrocephalus.

evidence.snippet: Case 2: a 16-year-old boy presented decreased visual acuity, papilledema, and morning headaches.
evidence.explanation: Papilledema as a documented presenting sign in an older child with a lateral-ventricular choroid plexus tumor and communicating hydrocephalus.

steps/18.description: Optic disc swelling from transmitted raised intracranial pressure; a classical sign in older children and adults whose sutures have fused and who therefore cannot decompress by head expansion.

evidence.snippet: Case 2: a 16-year-old boy presented decreased visual acuity, papilledema, and morning headaches.
evidence.explanation: Morning headache, the classical raised-intracranial-pressure pattern, as a presenting symptom of a choroid plexus tumor.

evidence.snippet: A 45-year-old woman presented with a 6-year history of headache and typical symptoms of normal-pressure hydrocephalus, including gait disturbance, urinary incontinence, and cognitive dysfunction, in addition to the more common symptoms of CPP, such as lower cranial nerve dysfunctions and ataxia.
evidence.explanation: Headache as the leading symptom in the adult, fourth-ventricular presentation.

steps/19.description: A presenting symptom of raised intracranial pressure, more prominent in older children and adults - the group in whom fourth-ventricular tumors predominate.

evidence.snippet: This child presented with macrocephaly, irritability, inability to roll over, and vomiting.
evidence.explanation: Vomiting as a documented presenting symptom alongside the other raised-pressure signs.

steps/20.description: Non-gastrointestinal vomiting from raised intracranial pressure, often with headache, and a common trigger for the imaging that reveals the tumor.

evidence.snippet: in addition to the more common symptoms of CPP, such as lower cranial nerve dysfunctions and ataxia
evidence.explanation: The authors identify ataxia and lower cranial nerve dysfunction as the more common symptoms of choroid plexus papilloma at this site.

steps/21.description: Cerebellar dysfunction from fourth-ventricular and cerebellopontine-angle tumors, the sites that predominate in adults.

evidence.snippet: We herein report a rare presentation of CPP in a 6-year-old Sudanese female child with seizures.
evidence.explanation: Documented seizure presentation of a lateral-ventricular choroid plexus papilloma; the authors themselves describe it as a rare presentation, consistent with the OCCASIONAL frequency band.

steps/22.description: A less common presentation, associated with supratentorial (lateral-ventricular) tumors and secondary parenchymal effects.

evidence.snippet: A 45-year-old woman presented with a 6-year history of headache and typical symptoms of normal-pressure hydrocephalus, including gait disturbance, urinary incontinence, and cognitive dysfunction
evidence.explanation: Gait disturbance as a documented presenting feature of an adult choroid plexus papilloma with communicating hydrocephalus.

evidence.snippet: The symptoms of normal-pressure hydrocephalus disappeared.
evidence.explanation: Resolution after tumour excision confirms the gait disturbance was tumour-driven rather than incidental.

steps/23.description: Gait impairment arises both from posterior-fossa/cerebellar involvement and, in adults with a communicating hydrocephalus, as part of a normal-pressure-hydrocephalus symptom complex that resolves after tumour removal.

evidence.snippet: in addition to the more common symptoms of CPP, such as lower cranial nerve dysfunctions and ataxia
evidence.explanation: The authors identify lower cranial nerve dysfunction as one of the more common symptoms of choroid plexus papilloma at this site.
